resources.string: New to kana? Choose Kana. Already read kana? Open Words or Grammar and select N5 on that page. Your existing selections stay unchanged.

Practice is not an unscored demo. In these three sections, advance from feedback with Next or I guessed. Saved answers update reviews; Back does not undo them. Opening questions or articles alone records no answer.
Choose Hiragana or Katakana, then Start under Kana → romaji (sounds written in Latin letters).
Combinations such as ちゅ unlock when both parts (ち and ゆ) are in Review (past initial learning), with FSRS stability of at least %1$d days.
Voiced and semi-voiced kana such as が or ぱ unlock when their plain base (か or は) is in Review with stability of at least %1$d days.
Stability estimates how long you can remember a character. It is not a calendar waiting period: keep practising when reviews are due.
Each script and each mode has its own progress and review schedule. Practise the components in the same script and mode you want to unlock. Already-started cards stay available.
First-time practice in each mode uses one shared daily Kana allowance across both scripts, separate from content study. Due reviews have no daily cap; Practice more can exceed the allowance.
To keep Romaji → kana questions distinct, ぢ/ヂ and づ/ヅ use di/du. Type the romaji also accepts ji/zu.
Start with Japanese → English. English → Japanese, Reading and picture modes use that progress. For Type it, first practise English → Japanese.
For each word, the earlier mode must be in Review (past initial learning), with at least %1$d recorded attempts and estimated stability of at least %2$s days.
Stability estimates how long you can remember the word; it is not a waiting period. Two correct answers alone do not guarantee an unlock. Continue the earlier mode when reviews are due.

A session also needs at least two suitable words in the selected deck; they do not both have to be unlocked. Reading uses words written with kanji, not kana-only words. Picture modes need suitable illustrations.

Unlocked counts describe progress in this deck, not today’s allowance or the number of answer choices. Each deck and mode keeps its own history. Already-started modes stay unlocked. Extra practice can also borrow eligible words from another deck.

Ready to learn counts first practice in each mode’s next finite batch, including content already introduced in another mode. Continue starts another batch within the shared allowance; Practice more can exceed it. Due reviews are not capped.
The limit applies separately to Kana and to content study. Each allowance follows your weekly rhythm and slows new introductions when reviews build up. Due reviews have no daily cap.
Kana shares one daily allowance across hiragana, katakana and all Kana modes.
Kanji, Words, Numbers & counters, Grammar and Listening share a separate allowance for the selected content repository.
Shared new-content allowance: %1$d unseen items left today. Learning another mode for previously introduced content does not spend this allowance. Mode counts are not added together.

New counts show available first-time practice, within its limits. Words and counters show ready-to-learn skills in each mode’s next finite batch; previously introduced content does not spend the new-content allowance again. Do not add mode or section counts. An allowance is a maximum, not a count of unlocked exercises; prerequisites or filters may leave nothing eligible.
Listening also limits new tasks and planned time. Starting a new scored task can reserve a shared content slot before an answer is recorded.

Cards, words and articles are downloaded from a public GitHub repository, so they can be corrected without an app update. The default is the author’s repository. Fork it on GitHub, edit the cards and articles in your fork, and enter your fork’s URL here to study your own version. Each repository keeps its own review progress.
